reading.body:
EdgeCore Silicon Valley publishes 72 MW of IT capacity across 540,000 square feet of technical space in Santa Clara County. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, this supports roughly 1,800 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a common colocation average, it supports roughly 7,200 racks.

The 540,000 square feet of technical space is large enough to accommodate dense cooling infrastructure alongside compute, which matters for high-heat GPU deployments. The operator does not publish a per-rack power envelope or a cooling specification, so the actual density and thermal design of this facility remain unclear from public sources.

The campus holds a single published certification, LEED, which addresses the efficiency of the building envelope and mechanical systems. LEED says nothing about uptime tier, redundancy architecture, or security posture, none of which are published on the operator's specification page.

Among the 103 data center facilities mapped in California, only five have published a megawatt figure. EdgeCore Silicon Valley's 72 MW ranks second among those five, representing 42 percent of the confirmed published capacity in the state. That share reflects sparse industry disclosure rather than a census of California's actual installed base, which is substantially larger than the 170 MW this site has read.
